At 0.33 us per dispatch these 964 are ALREADY batched -- 964 separate submissions would cost 151 SECONDS per token. THE SUBMISSION FLOOR DOES NOT REACH THIS WORKLOAD, which is the first time that has been checked at model scale rather than asserted either way.
FINDING_1_not_submission_bound.consequence_for_50_tps: eliminating ALL host overhead takes 30.19 ms to 29.87 ms = 33.5 TPS. DISPATCH FUSION CANNOT REACH 50 TPS HERE. Reaching 50 needs GPU time down to 20 ms, a 1.51x cut in the GPU work itself.

FINDING_2_ebpw_does_not_buy_decode_speed.reading: decode GPU time is NOT set by EBPW in this range, and the inversion is the informative part: the 2.60 body is a MIXED/HETERO codec and pays MORE unpack arithmetic. This independently reproduces at MODEL scale what ACCELERATOR_EXPERT_BATCH.json measured at TENSOR scale -- the native arm reaches only 161.9 GB/s against dense's 426.4 and is ARITHMETIC-BOUND ON THE UNPACK, not bandwidth-bound. Reading fewer bytes buys nothing when bytes are not the wall.
FINDING_2_ebpw_does_not_buy_decode_speed.consequence_for_S027_S028: the resurrection ladder's premise is that smaller is faster. Between 2.60 and 3.14 IT IS NOT -- density bought no decode speed and cost a little. A sub-bit body would have to win on UNPACK ARITHMETIC, not on byte count, and nothing here says it would.

what_this_DOES_NOT_establish: That EBPW never buys decode speed. THREE bodies over a 21% range on ONE runtime; a 1.25 or 0.53 BPW body is far outside this range and is NOT measured here.
That the unpack arithmetic cannot be made cheaper -- that is exactly the open kernel question, and this says where to point it, not what it will find.
Anything about prefill, batching or concurrency. This is single-stream decode only.
That 50 TPS is unreachable -- only that DISPATCH FUSION will not deliver it, since there is ~1% of wall there to reclaim.
